gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Noto Sans Tangsa opens wide on its round letters, with short ascender stems rising from tall, friendly bodies. And Gugi sits above it in a bolder voice, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, so a long paragraph of the plain sans feels easygoing.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tc: Distinctive is the right word for Gugi, whose lines are drawn like a plotter pen at a single weight. But Noto Sans TC does the quieter work, its outward-opening curves and generous counters making the sans the easier of the two to settle into.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Gugi's strokes never pinch at the curves, and that smooth, bold look is what you notice first. And Noto Sans Telugu follows with a high-set midline and counters that stay connected to the outside, so a long passage of the sans-serif moves along without fuss.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-thai: Gugi's crossbars are exactly as thick as its stems. Big and short is where it earns its keep, while Noto Sans Thai fills in with lowercase swollen like glass beads, rounded letters left open.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Gugi draws a tube-like stroke of constant width, and its lowercase stands nearly as tall as the capitals. But Noto Sans Thai Looped adds spacious gaps at its curve terminals, so the sans looks bold-ish and tall while still feeling clean beside it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Marker-pen boldness, then softness underneath. Gugi holds a steady, marker-like line weight, and Noto Sans Tifinagh lets its bowls fill the line like inflated shapes, so a longer read in the sans-serif feels open and inviting.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta brings a dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave a big gap. Gugi is best at a bold, distinctive heading with horizontals as heavy as its verticals, while Noto Sans Tirhuta is best at keeping the plain sans text contemporary and clean.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Chunky, smooth and unflickering. Gugi does its best work as a heading with no swelling where curves meet stems, while Noto Sans Ugaritic does its best as a sans with little gap between x-height and cap height and open letter mouths like unjoined chalk arcs.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-vai: Gugi is bold and distinctive, with no thick-thin flicker to snag the eye. Its strongest quality shows against Noto Sans Vai, a modern sans-serif whose words read as solid blocks rather than skylines.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Noto Sans Vithkuqi keeps its a, c, e and s open in the throat, with only a minimal step from capital to lowercase. Gugi's bold, distinctive heading sits above, and the sans-serif body reads smoothly across a longer stretch.
